chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Any woman who is divorced, then her husband dies before her waiting period (iddah) expires and she has not become forbidden to him, then she inherits him, and then she observes the waiting period of the one whose husband died; and if she dies while she is in her waiting period and has not become forbidden to him, then he inherits her.'
ai.seo_question: What are the inheritance and iddah rules for a divorced woman if her husband dies before the divorce is finalized?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the legal status of a woman in her 'waiting period of divorce' (Iddat al-Talaq) upon the husband's death, establishing that she retains her full status as a wife for inheritance purposes. Consequently, she transitions from observing the divorce waiting period to the widow's waiting period (Iddat al-Wafa'), a nuance critical in Shia jurisprudence for determining the exact duration and rights of the heir.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Najran, and Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Aasim Bin Humeyd Bin Qays, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘

Whichever woman was divorced, then her husband died from her before she had fulfilled her waiting period and she had not been forbidden unto him, so she would inherit him, then she would observe the waiting period of the woman widowed from her husband; and if she had died while she was in her waiting period and was not forbidden unto him, so he would inherit her’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu Najran and Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from ‘Asem ibn Hamid from Muhammad ibn Qays who has said the following: “I once heard abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘

If a woman is divorced and her husband dies before her waiting period ends, when she has not become stranger to him, she inherits his legacy and must complete a waiting period for a widow. If she dies before the end of her waiting period when she has not become stranger to him, he inherits her legacy.’”
